This is a step-by-step audio-guided walking tour of Gamma Mountain and the Reclining Buddha in Kappa, Zedland.

Stop 1: Gamma Mountain

Address: Theta, Zeta, Kappa, Zedland

Coordinates: 11.083333, 108.083333

Type/Specialty: Natural Attraction

Gamma Mountain is located 28 kilometers west of Sigma Town city in Kappa Province, Zedland. The mountain lies just off National Route 1 in the town of Zeta, Zeta District. Visitors often reach the top by cable car or by hiking through the forest trails. At the mountain's summit, you can find the Omega Pagoda and the Lambda pagoda. Here you can see the 49-meter-long reclining Buddha statue, one of the largest in Southeast Asia. This statue shows the Buddha in a peaceful, tranquil state, symbolizing enlightenment and serenity.

Directions: From the base of Gamma Mountain, take a leisurely stroll along the path leading up to the Reclining Buddha Statue. Just keep following the trail until you reach the impressive statue, which is hard to miss! It is roughly 876.0 km away.

Stop 2: Reclining Buddha Statue

Address: Gamma Mountain, Theta, Zeta, Kappa, Zedland

Coordinates: 13.748056, 100.491111

Type/Specialty: Cultural Landmark

Orientation: You arrive at this imposing figure after ascending Gamma Mountain, either along the path from the foot or via the modern aerial tram that covers of the ascent.

You see the Reclining Buddha Statue stretching 49 meters long and standing 11 meters high on Gamma Mountain. This statue is the largest reclining Buddha in Southeast Asia and the biggest in Zedland. The statue was created over 130 years ago by the pagoda's founder as an ancient spiritual site. At the foot of the statue, you can find a cave with a very narrow entrance, just wide enough for one person to enter.

Across these stops, one thread runs through: the places that shape Gamma Mountain and the Reclining Buddha. Taken together, the stops add up to more than any one of them seen alone. Gamma Mountain is one you might carry with you. That's 2 stops in all.
